combat_wing: 1st CBW, high group (lead 91st, low 381st); Air Commander Lt Col Milton (briefing outline, 351-02)
dispatched_notes: 351-02 (group mission page transcribing the operations, S-2 and statistical reports): 18 aircraft assigned and took off, 0 failed to take off, 8 abortive, 10 attacked the target, 1 missing (42-6096); casualties ten MIA and five wounded. 351-05 (303rd BG mission 78 summary) and 351-06 (IWM mission page) list 351BG as 16 aircraft in the 1st Air Division table; recorded here as a conflict. The load list database has 18 aircraft for mission 49.

aircraft.formation_position: Group lead (Maj. J.R. Blaylock, Group Leader; Capt. W. Stockman lead navigator; 1st Lt. J.O. Bradley bombardier). Lead position on Combat Report Form diagram.
aircraft.notes: Crew from the 351st BG crew loading-list database (351-01, mission 49). Squadron given is the crew's squadron per the load list; code letters, block and nickname are for the aircraft per 351-03 and are not confirmed for this date (aircraft were often flown by other squadrons' crews). Nickname per 351-03 only: 'The Duchess' (not evidenced for 14 Oct 1943). One of the nine aircraft that completed the mission and returned: six landed at base, three at Kenley and Gravesend (which three not identified). 351-02 reports five wounded aboard returning aircraft; names not found. Take-off 1026, landed 1750 per Combat Bombing Flight Record. Lead ship hit by flak and 20mm; one 20mm shell entered the cockpit behind the pilot's head and fell unexploded (Group Leader's narrative). Capt. Orville Oldham Jr. (508th) in tail position, consistent with a formation-control officer.

aircraft.loss_details: 351-02 S-2 narrative: lost just after the target; #2 engine already feathered when #4 was knocked out by a rocket shell and caught fire; pilot fell out of formation; the ship caught fire and two parachutes were seen before it blew up. Operations narrative: 'seen to blow up over the target'. 351-03: crashed at Schweinfurt. Load list: 9 POW, 1 KIA (S/Sgt Granville R. Brown).

research_gaps: Which of 42-3509 (Argiropolus) and 42-29863 (Hathaway) flew over the target is unresolved (load list vs Combat Report Form diagram).
The five men wounded on returning aircraft are not named in the sources seen; all returning crew are recorded as 'returned'.
Which three of the nine returning bombers landed at Kenley/Gravesend is not identified.
Reasons for each of the eight aborts are not linked to specific aircraft.

Crew data come from the 351st.org load-list database (a transcription of the group's crew loading lists); the original loading-list images were not inspected, so individual crew are PROBABLE except the Crismon crew, which is cross-checked against 351-03.
Squadron codes, blocks and nicknames are from b17flyingfortress.de (351-03) only and refer to the aircraft's assigned squadron; none confirmed for 14 Oct 1943.
42-30135 'Trouble Shooter' (MACR 855), sometimes attributed to the 351st/511th for this date, was with the 95th BG/334th BS (BG-H) by 14 Oct 1943 per 351-03 and is excluded here.
IWM/americanairmuseum person pages not checked for the Crismon crew (rate-limited/blocked).

Searched: 351st.org load-list database (mission 49 and all 18 aircraft), 351st.org mission 49 page and Combat Report Form image, b17flyingfortress.de pages for all 18 serials and its 14-10-1943 loss list, 303rd BG mission 78 PDF, IWM mission page VIII BC 115.
